**🟢 Correct** — `String.fromEnvironment` is a compile-time constant in Dart, so `const _relayUrlsEnv` is valid. The `--dart-define` flag propagates it correctly at build time.

**🟢 Correct** — Dart's `Uri` parser only applies default ports for `http`/`https`. For `ws://localhost` (no explicit port), `uri.port` returns `0`, so the fallback `(uri.scheme == 'wss' ? 443 : 80)` is reached and is correct.

issue.title: Support Android in integration tests
issue.body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/dd1ac80777d20141b7bd33d3f22d917f040b45872cfbc5ca53d126f3f81f30ba.jpg) `just int-test` now runs on Android. ## What changed - `_resolve-device` falls back to `adb devices` when no booted iOS simulator is found, and skips `xcrun` on hosts where it isn't installed (so Linux works too). - `int-test` auto-injects public Nostr relays through `--dart-define=WHITENOISE_INTEGRATION_RELAYS=...` when the resolved device is an Android one. The emulator can't reach the host's localhost, so the local docker relays aren't usable there. - `integration_test/_support/app_setup.dart` reads the relay list from that dart-define (default: the same two localhost relays as before), and the TCP precheck now no-ops for non-localhost URLs. The iOS path is unchanged, and either platform can override the relay list with `WHITENOISE_INTEGRATION_RELAYS=...`. ## Why The marmot colony hibernates near the host, but our Android sibling lives one virtual network away (it can't hear the local relays burrowing at `127.0.0.1`). So when the Android marmot wants to chat, we point it at the public relays already used in production: `nos.lol`, `relay.primal.net`, `relay.damus.io`. ## How to use ```bash # iOS simulator (unchanged) just int-test # Android emulator (auto-detected, auto-uses public relays) just int-test # Override relays on any platform WHITENOISE_INTEGRATION_RELAYS=wss://my.relay just int-test ``` --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Tests** * Integration tests now support configurable relay URLs via environment variable * Device detection expanded to include both iOS simulators and connected Android devices * Local relay connectivity checks enhanced to work with any configured relay URL [![Review Change Stack](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/review-stack-in-coderabbit-ui.svg)](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/marmot-protocol/whitenoise/pull/690?utm_source=github_walkthrough&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=change_stack)

issue.title: fix: route user-tag taps to the group member screen for members
issue.body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/3bc2fd2a26b31776a66740df4df014b23b1e1319feacd49e667f722f9a4e3f1d.png)

Closes #681.

Tapping an @-mention inside a chat bubble used to open the start-chat shade, even when the tagged marmot was already in the group. Now the bubble checks the group roster and routes to the group member shade for members, keeping the start-chat shade for non-members and DMs.

Since the chat screen already loads the member list once via `useGroupMembers`, the bubble gets a memoized `Set<String>` instead of fetching members per bubble. That keeps the "don't fetch in every chat bubble" line from the issue satisfied.

For consistency, the start-chat shade now anchors to the top of the screen, matching the group member shade. Both shades slide in from the same spot.

`@dannym-arx` Love the pixel art marmots! 🐾 Here's the full review:

---

## Review of PR `#689` — Long-press QR code to share as image

### `lib/screens/share_profile_screen.dart`

---

**🔴 Missing `name` on `XFile.fromData`**

```dart
files: [XFile.fromData(byteData.buffer.asUint8List(), mimeType: 'image/png')],
```

`XFile.fromData` without a `name` argument leaves the file nameless. On iOS the share sheet and on Android some targets (e.g. Google Photos, email) will show a blank filename or fail silently. Suggest:

```dart
files: [
  XFile.fromData(
    byteData.buffer.asUint8List(),
    name: 'qr_code.png',
    mimeType: 'image/png',
  ),
],
```

---

**🟡 No guard against concurrent invocations of `captureAndShareQr()`**

`onLongPressStart` is theoretically callable while a previous `captureAndShareQr()` is still in-flight (e.g. user releases just before the 1 500 ms mark and re-presses). Both coroutines share `isHolding` state, and if both are live at the moment of `dotCount.value = 3`, both will attempt to call `SharePlus.instance.share(...)`. A simple `isCapturing` ref prevents this:

```dart
final isCapturing = useRef(false);

Future<void> captureAndShareQr() async {
  if (isCapturing.value) return;
  isCapturing.value = true;
  try {
    // ... existing logic
  } finally {
    isCapturing.value = false;
  }
}
```

---

**🟡 Error path doesn't reset animation/dot counter**

In the `catch` block only `showErrorNotice` is called. If the error fires while the user is still holding (rare but possible for very fast capture failures), the dots and grey tint remain active until `onLongPressEnd` fires. Since you already have `onLongPressEnd` resetting state this is partially mitigated, but an explicit reset in the catch is more defensive:

```dart
} catch (e) {
  if (isMounted.value) {
    dotCount.value = 0;
    qrColorAnim.reverse();
    showErrorNotice(errorMessage);
  }
}
```

---

**🟡 Instruction label shown as status label**

```dart
isHolding.value
    ? '${context.l10n.holdToShareQrCode}${'.' * dotCount.value}'
    : context.l10n.scanToConnect,
```

`holdToShareQrCode` = "Hold to share QR code" is an instruction. Once the user *is* holding, the text should act as a progress/status indicator instead. Consider a second key like `sharingQrCode` ("Sharing…" or "Keep holding…") for the active state, or at minimum separate the label from the dot counter so the dots alone signal progress.

---

**🟢 Positive observations**

- `errorMessage` is captured before any `await`, so `context` is never used across a suspension point. ✓  
- `isMounted` ref + guard at every suspension point is correct and thorough. ✓  
- `captureFuture` is fired before the first `await Future.delayed`, so the shared PNG captures the last full-color rasterized frame as intended. ✓  
- `onLongPressCancel` and `onLongPressEnd` both reverse the animation and reset dots — no stuck gray states. ✓  
- `qrRepaintKey` is correctly placed *inside* the `GestureDetector` but the boundary encloses only the QR, not the gesture layer. ✓  

---

### Localization files

All 10 locale files (`de`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `it`, `pt`, `ru`, `tr`, `zh`, `zh_Hant`) provide both `holdToShareQrCode` and `shareQrCodeError`. Translations look natural and consistent. ✓

---

### Summary

| Severity | Issue |
|---|---|
| 🔴 High | `XFile.fromData` missing `name: 'qr_code.png'` — affects share sheet on iOS & some Android targets |
| 🟡 Medium | No concurrent-invocation guard on `captureAndShareQr()` |
| 🟡 Medium | `catch` block doesn't reset dot/animation state |
| 🟡 Medium | "Hold to share" label semantics during active hold |

The core logic is solid and the UX idea is great — just the `XFile` filename is a must-fix before shipping. 🐾

Teams are shipping faster than ever with AI, but engineers are merging changes that neither they nor their reviewers fully understand, leading to bugs in production and overwhelming cognitive debt.

Stage is a new code review platform built for today’s fast moving teams. Instead of forcing readers to piece things together from unorganized diffs, Stage breaks changes down into structured chapters so teams can understand what's happening and ship with confidence.
